Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

slightly adverb

also a little (in degree), somewhat, a bit (more, less), slightly more, slightly less

classical

Caes. BG 6.9: paulum suprā eum locum (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Agr. 2.85: paulum differre (Lewis & Short)

paulum

adverb: the accusative of paulus

slightly, a little (with verbs and prepositions)

With verbs and prepositions: paulum differre, to differ slightly; paulum suprā, slightly above. With a comparative Latin uses the ablative paulō instead (next). The same word is the noun “a little” of an amount (see a little).

Other words

  • paulō (+ comparative) — slightly (more, less, earlier)

    ablative of the degree of difference, with a comparative or with ante, post · also used · classical · Cic. Quinct. 11: paulō minus cōnsīderātus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Or. 82: līberius paulō (Lewis & Short)

    Latin measures the difference by the ablative: paulō major, slightly bigger; paulō ante, a little earlier (Lewis & Short).

  • leviter — slightly (ill, hurt, bent)

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.83: quī leviter aegrōtantēs lēniter cūrant (Lewis & Short); Cic. Inv. 2.154: leviter saucius (Lewis & Short)

    Of a condition that is slight, not grave: leviter aegrōtāre, to be slightly ill; leviter saucius, slightly wounded. This is its usual sense in Cicero; the literal “lightly, not heavily” is rare (Lewis & Short).

  • subtristis, subtriste — slightly sad

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Ter. And. 447: Subtristis vīsus est esse aliquantulum mihi.

    (vōx cōmica: Ter.; in ōrātiōne solūtā rāra)

    Latin can say “slightly” with the prefix sub-: subtristis, a little sad, is Terence’s (Lewis & Short: ante- and post-classical). Use the compounds the dictionary gives rather than coining new ones.

Examples

  • quī leviter aegrōtantēs lēniter cūrant

    (doctors) who treat the slightly ill gentlyCic. Off. 1.83 (Lewis & Short)

  • Subtristis vīsus est esse aliquantulum mihi.

    He seemed to me a little on the sad side.Ter. And. 447

  • paulō minus cōnsīderātus

    slightly less carefulCic. Quinct. 11 (Lewis & Short)

  • Paulō major est quam tū.

    He’s slightly bigger than you.composed

See also a little, quite, very, almost.
